standard_prerequisites.name: Standard Young tableaux of shape (k_1,k_2)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Syt(k_1,k_2) is the set of standard Young tableaux with two rows of lengths k_1 >= k_2, filled with 1,...,k_1+k_2 increasingly along rows and columns.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both sides of the displayed identity are sets of such tableaux, and the map is defined on entries.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Des(T) is the set of i such that i+1 appears in a strictly lower row than i in T.
standard_prerequisites.use: The condition Des(T) contains J is what is transported by the bijection.

core_obligations: Define the map on tableaux: send T in Syt(k_1,k_2) with Des(T) containing J to the tableau T' in Syt(k_1+1,k_2+1) given by T'_{1,1} = 1, T'_{2,1} = 2 and T'_{i,j+1} = T_{i,j} + 2 for j in [k_i] (source line 468).
Describe the construction as increasing every entry of T by 2 and then inserting a new leftmost column with the letters 1 and 2 (source line 468).
Check that the map is injective, that T' is a standard Young tableau of the larger shape, and that Des(T') contains {1} union (J+2) (source line 468).
Show surjectivity onto the tableaux T' of the larger shape with Des(T') containing {1} union (J+2) by reading the construction backwards, which exhibits the two-sided inverse (source line 468).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the map on tableaux by shifting all entries by 2 and inserting a leftmost column.
Verify injectivity, the descent condition, and the inverse construction for surjectivity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:remove first descent from syt` at source lines 459-466: for integers k_1 >= k_2 >= 0 and a set J contained in [k_1+k_2-1], the number of two-row standard Young tableaux of shape (k_1,k_2) whose descent set contains J equals the number of such tableaux of shape (k_1+1,k_2+1) whose descent set contains {1} union (J+2). The author's proof (source lines 467-469) is a single paragraph, but it is an explicit bijection rather than a counting argument: the map shifts every entry by 2 and inserts a leftmost column carrying 1 and 2 (line 468), and the proof has to verify three separate properties of this map, namely injectivity, the fact that the image is again a standard Young tableau with the required descent condition, and the fact that the construction can be read backwards to recover any tableau of the larger shape with that descent condition. The statement gives only the resulting cardinality identity, and the shape of the inserted column is what the reader has to discover.
